result:
I would give every person—no matter where they are born or who they are—the reliable opportunity to learn.

Why that single change?

1. Cascading benefits  
   • Health: People who can read, reason, and access information make better choices about nutrition, disease prevention, and parenting.  
   • Economy: Education expands skills, drives innovation, and lifts communities out of poverty.  
   • Environment: Understanding science fosters stewardship of the planet.  
   • Governance: An informed public is harder to deceive and more inclined to defend human rights and peaceful solutions.

2. Self-reinforcing progress  
   Quality education fuels the very capacities—critical thinking, empathy, collaboration—that help societies keep improving education itself, creating a virtuous cycle.

3. Respect for human autonomy  
   Instead of imposing a particular solution from the outside, education equips people to identify and solve their own problems in ways that fit their culture and circumstances.

In short, if everyone had meaningful access to learning, many other global challenges—inequality, conflict, health crises, environmental decline—would become far easier to solve, because every community would have the knowledge and tools to tackle them.
